entries.evidence:
D2.65 two-step adjudication on the full-family-stream sample.
Step 1: R converges to 230 exactly (trace 241.18 -> 229 -> 230 -> 230) and stays there at n.cyc = 200 -- a stationary point that is worse than ours, the PE2 disposition.
Step 2: R's own dWARING at our coefficients returns 228.75 against our 228.809581 (rel 2.6e-04): the two densities agree to within a rounding-scale difference and both put our point below R's 230.  Perturbing either coefficient by 1e-3 raises our deviance.
Stream discipline: numbers bind to the full-family sample stream.

entries.detail: R's reported deviance 208.385 is scored with a density that is not elementwise (R's own density evaluated elementwise gives 209.509); ours 209.285 is below that
entries.evidence: D2.85.  R dZANBI normalises with fy0 <- dNBI(0, mu=mu, sigma=sigma, log=TRUE),and R dNBI does NOT recycle the scalar x against a vector mu: measured onlive R, length(dNBI(0, mu=c(2,8), sigma=c(0.1,0.1), log=TRUE)) is 1, not 2(the value is f0 at the first mu).  So the whole vector shares one f0, whileour implementation evaluates each observation own -- which is what dZANBIown source formula says it should do.  On the scanner sample(sigma -> 0.0347, nu = 0.0625) R reports 208.384659; evaluating theelementwise formula at R own fitted mu gives 209.50928, i.e. R number is1.12 too low.  Our fit stop

entries.evidence: D2.86. Our own fit stops at 205.077211, below that reference.
